```
3. Objective and optimizer health
Loss windows follow observed epoch cadence. Partial table-coverage epoch losses are retained in tables, without endpoint crosses. The selected receipt determines the included bases; a targeted TabPFN repair cohort does not imply missing TabICLv2 research runs. Numerical and clipping checks are tabulated; the shared schedule is shown once. Negative density NLL can be valid. Peak clipped fraction is the largest recorded epoch fraction, not the trial-wide fraction.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 13 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: lgd_pilot_loss_lgd
LGD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 6 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.
```

```
2. Credit transfer and non-credit retention
Historical objective provenance limits comparison with the corrected main grid. Missing milestones remain gaps; these pilots do not identify a universal optimum.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_updates
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_updates
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

3. Row exposure
The same milestone scores are plotted against cumulative processed row exposures, which include repeated observations.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_processed_rows
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_processed_rows
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

5. Objective, schedule and parameter movement
Losses retain separate architecture scales. Optimizer and parameter measurements are tabulated, and common learning-rate schedules share a figure.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 400 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.
```

## experiment0/04_auxiliary_experiments

```
Experiment 0: auxiliary experiment checks

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
These controls establish execution and measurement validity. They do not test whether credit-domain specialization improves generalization.

1. Planned checks
52 six-update arms across eight GPU tasks: 36 uninterrupted arms and 16 interrupted/resumed comparisons. LGD seed-42 one-sample also serves as the stratified sampling control. PD has a separate stratified control. The tiny 256-row cap and smoke retention panel bound debugging cost.
```

```
2. Loss, optimization and predictive learning curves
Data loss excludes anchoring: PD query cross-entropy; TabPFN LGD bar-distribution NLL; TabICLv2 LGD mean quantile pinball loss. Equal partition and configuration weights apply to optimization curves; monitoring first gives each table equal weight. Native objective scales remain separate by architecture. Missing support produces gaps.

Figure: pd_optimization_dashboard_pd_tabicl-v2
PD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

PD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: pd_monitor_dashboard_pd_test
PD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_monitor_dashboard_pd_ood
PD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

3. How training choices change the dynamics
Differences are alternative minus reference. References are no L2-SP, all-parameter updates and LR 3e-7. Model-specific loss scales are never pooled; differences in gradient norm are optimization diagnostics, not predictive benefits. Base-model predictive comparisons are shown in the results notebook.

Figure: pd_factor_dashboard_pd_l2sp_lambda_tabicl-v2
PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: pd_factor_dashboard_pd_frozen_v2.6
PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

4. Applied learning-rate schedule
PD and LGD use the same configured schedule, shown once in the PD training notebook. Initialization has zero rate; log axes only show positive rates.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

5. Parameter movement
Anchored displacement depends on the trainable subset. Freezing leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; movement is not evidence of causal predictive improvement.

Figure: pd_trainable_fraction_pd
PD. Trainable parameters divided by total model parameters for each base and adaptation mode. Counts are taken from observed trial provenance; median counts are used where recipes repeat a model. The frozen condition leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; it is not the same parameter subset across architectures.

6. Resources, cost and scope
518,784 parameter-tensor measurements; 62,987 resource samples.
GPU counter status: gpu_status
sampled    62987
Device samples are not integrated energy or billed allocation time. The main grid has one training seed; table and partition variation does not estimate seed robustness.

Figure: pd_resource_dashboard_pd
PD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.
```

```
0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.

2. Loss, optimization and predictive learning curves
Data loss excludes anchoring: PD query cross-entropy; TabPFN LGD bar-distribution NLL; TabICLv2 LGD mean quantile pinball loss. Equal partition and configuration weights apply to optimization curves; monitoring first gives each table equal weight. Native objective scales remain separate by architecture. Missing support produces gaps.

Figure: lgd_optimization_dashboard_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: lgd_optimization_dashboard_lgd_v2
LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: lgd_optimization_dashboard_lgd_v3
LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: lgd_monitor_dashboard_lgd_test
LGD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_monitor_dashboard_lgd_ood
LGD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

3. How training choices change the dynamics
Differences are alternative minus reference. References are no L2-SP, all-parameter updates and LR 3e-7. Model-specific loss scales are never pooled; differences in gradient norm are optimization diagnostics, not predictive benefits. Base-model predictive comparisons are shown in the results notebook.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_l2sp_lambda_tabicl-v2
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_frozen_v2
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_frozen_v2.6
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

5. Parameter movement
Anchored displacement depends on the trainable subset. Freezing leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; movement is not evidence of causal predictive improvement.

LGD. Trainable parameters divided by total model parameters for each base and adaptation mode. Counts are taken from observed trial provenance; median counts are used where recipes repeat a model. The frozen condition leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; it is not the same parameter subset across architectures.

Figure: lgd_resource_dashboard_lgd
LGD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.
```

```
Experiment 1: PD outcomes and evaluation

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does stronger credit-domain adaptation improve transfer to excluded credit tables, and what does it preserve or lose on the non-credit panel? The grid is descriptive; the highest test score is not a selected deployment result.

5. Probability quality, calibration and thresholds
Brier score combines discrimination and calibration; ECE depends on its bins. The calibration overview compares the same tables across raw, Platt and isotonic scores; reliability examples are selected by dataset size independently of performance.
Raw predictions are paired by dataset, training partition, outer fold and row. All five folds and exactly matching test rows/targets are required. Mean error is prediction minus observed target: positive means overprediction. Its absolute value can conceal offsetting subgroup errors. Brier/MSE and prediction movement pool rows within each table; tables receive equal weight in summaries. These are observed out-of-fold diagnostics, not squared theoretical bias or context variance.

Figure: pd_reference_roc_auc_1
PD. Dataset-level AUC changes for the predefined full-update recipe, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003, relative to each model's untuned weights. Pairing occurs within outer folds and requires all five folds. Positive values indicate improvement; only RMSE is expressed as a fractional reduction.

Figure: pd_calibration_overview
PD. Changes in outer-test Brier score and expected calibration error (ECE) for the predefined full-update reference (LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, one-sample training) relative to its untuned base. Positive reductions favor continued pretraining (CPT). Raw probabilities and validation-fitted Platt and isotonic calibration use a common dataset cohort within each base: all six scores require the same five completed, matched outer folds. Diamonds show equal-dataset means; horizontal lines span dataset quartiles, not confidence intervals. ECE depends on the binning scheme.

Figure: pd_reliability_tabicl-v2_1
PD. Raw, Platt-scaled and isotonic positive-class reliability for the predefined full-update reference (LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, one-sample training) and its untuned base. Rows identify datasets and columns identify calibration methods. Each populated panel requires bin records from the same five completed outer folds for both models; missing panels are labeled. Ten equal-width bins pool outer-test counts within the dataset; empty bins are omitted and bin counts are retained in the text summary. Calibrators are fitted only on inner validation rows. The diagonal denotes agreement of predicted and observed probabilities; these curves have no uncertainty intervals. Examples are chosen at evenly spaced dataset-size ranks (smallest and largest when two are shown), using total outer-test row counts independently of model scores. They illustrate calibration shapes rather than the typical treatment effect.

They illustrate calibration shapes rather than the typical treatment effect.

Figure: pd_reliability_v2.6_1
PD. Raw, Platt-scaled and isotonic positive-class reliability for the predefined full-update reference (LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, one-sample training) and its untuned base. Rows identify datasets and columns identify calibration methods. Each populated panel requires bin records from the same five completed outer folds for both models; missing panels are labeled. Ten equal-width bins pool outer-test counts within the dataset; empty bins are omitted and bin counts are retained in the text summary. Calibrators are fitted only on inner validation rows. The diagonal denotes agreement of predicted and observed probabilities; these curves have no uncertainty intervals. Examples are chosen at evenly spaced dataset-size ranks (smallest and largest when two are shown), using total outer-test row counts independently of model scores. They illustrate calibration shapes rather than the typical treatment effect.

Figure: pd_reliability_v3_1
PD. Raw, Platt-scaled and isotonic positive-class reliability for the predefined full-update reference (LR 3e-7, L2-SP 0.003, one-sample training) and its untuned base. Rows identify datasets and columns identify calibration methods. Each populated panel requires bin records from the same five completed outer folds for both models; missing panels are labeled. Ten equal-width bins pool outer-test counts within the dataset; empty bins are omitted and bin counts are retained in the text summary. Calibrators are fitted only on inner validation rows. The diagonal denotes agreement of predicted and observed probabilities; these curves have no uncertainty intervals. Examples are chosen at evenly spaced dataset-size ranks (smallest and largest when two are shown), using total outer-test row counts independently of model scores. They illustrate calibration shapes rather than the typical treatment effect.

6. Classical controls, non-credit retention and cost
One main training seed and overlapping adaptation corpora limit independence claims. The non-credit panel is finite and original pretraining overlap is unverified. No recipe winner is treated as an unbiased estimate of future generalization.
```

## experiment1/04_results_lgd

```
Experiment 1: LGD outcomes and evaluation

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does stronger credit-domain adaptation improve transfer to excluded credit tables, and what does it preserve or lose on the non-credit panel? The grid is descriptive; the highest test score is not a selected deployment result.

1. Evidence and benchmark eligibility
Run cpt_main_v5; LGD; 256 planned trials; target 10,000 successful updates.
status
OK    256
1536 trajectory records; 8520 benchmark fold records.
PENDING means no recorded outcome; it can include running or queued work. This is not live scheduler state.

Open marks freeze the backbone; filled marks update all normally trainable parameters. Colors denote learning rates and marker shapes denote L2-SP. These are fixed-context monitoring scores, not final five-fold estimates.

Figure: lgd_endpoint_dashboard_lgd_means
LGD. Initial and post-finetuning scores for each completed configuration. Each dot averages the four partition means with equal partition weight; incomplete configurations are omitted. Scores first average available held-out tables within each partition. Colors distinguish learning rates and marker shapes distinguish anchoring. Open marks freeze the transformer backbone; filled marks update all parameters. The diagonal indicates unchanged score. These fixed-context monitors do not substitute for final five-fold benchmark scores.

LGD. Initial and post-finetuning scores for each completed configuration. Labels P1–P4 above the point columns identify training-dataset partitions; each configuration retains its own point. Scores first average available held-out tables within each partition. Colors distinguish learning rates and marker shapes distinguish anchoring. Open marks freeze the transformer backbone; filled marks update all parameters. The diagonal indicates unchanged score. These fixed-context monitors do not substitute for final five-fold benchmark scores.

Match every other setting and dataset before averaging contrasts. Base averages are descriptive, not causal model comparisons. Probability accuracy is assessed by Brier score when paired measurements exist; missing measurements are not inferred.

LGD. Conditional differences match dataset and every other configuration setting before averaging within model. Peak-learning-rate contrasts use LR 3e-7 as reference. The base-model panel averages configuration effects relative to each model's own initialization; it is descriptive rather than a causal architecture contrast. Positive values favor the alternative setting. Dataset and configuration support are retained in the accompanying tables.

5. Regression errors and prediction shifts
RMSE and MAE summarize prediction errors, while R2 compares squared error with a constant predictor. Distributional calibration requires stored predictive distributions rather than point errors.
Raw predictions are paired by dataset, training partition, outer fold and row. All five folds and exactly matching test rows/targets are required. Mean error is prediction minus observed target: positive means overprediction. Its absolute value can conceal offsetting subgroup errors. Brier/MSE and prediction movement pool rows within each table; tables receive equal weight in summaries. These are observed out-of-fold diagnostics, not squared theoretical bias or context variance.

6. Classical controls, non-credit retention and cost
One main training seed and overlapping adaptation corpora limit independence claims. The non-credit panel is finite and original pretraining overlap is unverified. No recipe winner is treated as an unbiased estimate of future generalization.
```

## experiment2/01_training

```
Experiment 2: seed sensitivity during training

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does the fixed credit-CPT recipe change individual predictions and transfer outcomes when only training randomness changes? Two seeds measure sensitivity, not a reliable variance distribution.

1. Reference recipe and training coverage
Seed 42 reuses the predefined main reference; seed 43 has 16 trials per task. Pending status is not live scheduler state.

Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Figure: pd_process_pd_v2
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2.6
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v3
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2.6
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v3
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

3. Credit transfer and non-credit retention through training
Non-credit curves require all four matched partitions per dataset and retain the baseline dataset cohort. These small-context monitors are separate from final five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_credit_seeds
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_credit_seeds
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_ood_seeds
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_resource_dashboard_pd
PD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.

Figure: pd_movement_pd_tabicl-v2
PD. Complementary summaries of parameter movement. Whole-model drift is norm weighted; tensor movement first takes the median across anchored tensors within a trial. Curves then take medians across available recipes and partitions within each adaptation arm; counts are reported alongside values. Both quantities use their recorded milestones. Changing trial support can affect these descriptive curves.

Figure: lgd_resource_dashboard_lgd
LGD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.
```

## experiment2/02_results

```
Experiment 2: paired seed outcomes

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does the fixed credit-CPT recipe change individual predictions and transfer outcomes when only training randomness changes? Two seeds measure sensitivity, not a reliable variance distribution.

1. Checkpoint and benchmark coverage
Five complete outer folds and the matching untuned reference are required for each benchmark effect. Evaluation seed 99 is shared; training seed changes only continued pretraining.

2. Final benchmark seed comparison
Pair partition/dataset observations before averaging. Non-credit datasets require all four paired training partitions; no incomplete counterpart is replaced by another fold.

Figure: pd_seed_benchmark_credit
PD. Held-out credit: five-fold benchmark effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: pd_seed_benchmark_ood
PD. Non-credit retention: five-fold benchmark effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: lgd_seed_benchmark_credit
LGD. Held-out credit: five-fold benchmark effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Fractional RMSE reduction (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: lgd_seed_benchmark_ood
LGD. Non-credit retention: five-fold benchmark effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Fractional RMSE reduction (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

3. Probability quality, calibration and error metrics
Brier score and log loss assess probability quality; ECE is a bin-dependent calibration diagnostic. F1 thresholds and Platt/isotonic calibration use validation rows only. Unsupported or incomplete metrics stay absent. Classical and untuned model scores provide context.
Raw predictions are paired by dataset, training partition, outer fold and row. All five folds and exactly matching test rows/targets are required. Mean error is prediction minus observed target: positive means overprediction. Its absolute value can conceal offsetting subgroup errors. Brier/MSE and prediction movement pool rows within each table; tables receive equal weight in summaries. These are observed out-of-fold diagnostics, not squared theoretical bias or context variance.

4. Endpoint monitors as supporting evidence
Monitor and benchmark figures have distinct identities, captions and data sources. Their score differences are not estimates of seed sensitivity.

Figure: pd_seed_monitor_credit
PD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: pd_seed_monitor_ood
PD. Non-credit retention: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: lgd_seed_monitor_credit
LGD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in R² (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: lgd_seed_monitor_ood
LGD. Non-credit retention: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in R² (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.
```

## experiment3/01_training

```
Experiment 3: sampling and accumulation during training

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does additional row exposure or different update weighting improve credit-CPT outcomes enough to justify its cost? Equal optimizer updates do not match computation.

1. Protocol coverage
There are 48 trials per task. A saved interruption is recoverable progress, not a completed checkpoint or numerical failure.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2.6
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v3
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2.6
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v3
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_credit_updates
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_ood_updates
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

4. Row exposure and matched cost
Exposure counts repeated rows. No interpolation claims equal row or compute budgets. Cost comparisons require all three protocols for a partition; absolute costs accompany their ratios.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_credit_rows
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_sampling_costs
PD. Ratios to the one-sample trial matched on base, recipe and dataset partition. Only partitions with all three completed protocols enter. Points are partition means and segments are partition interquartile ranges, not uncertainty intervals. Trial time includes recorded monitoring and excludes queueing; it is not billed GPU allocation time. Row exposure counts repeated rows. Absolute costs and peak memory accompany the ratios.

LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

5. Resource utilization and parameter movement
Recorded GPU/process counters and anchored displacement describe the execution. They do not establish energy consumption or causal effects of parameter movement.

Figure: pd_resource_dashboard_pd
PD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.

Figure: pd_movement_pd_tabicl-v2
PD. Complementary summaries of parameter movement. Whole-model drift is norm weighted; tensor movement first takes the median across anchored tensors within a trial. Curves then take medians across available recipes and partitions within each adaptation arm; counts are reported alongside values. Both quantities use their recorded milestones. Changing trial support can affect these descriptive curves.

Figure: lgd_resource_dashboard_lgd
LGD. Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.
```

```
Experiment 3: sampling and accumulation outcomes

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does additional row exposure or different update weighting improve credit-CPT outcomes enough to justify its cost? Equal optimizer updates do not match computation.

PD. Non-credit retention: five-fold benchmark effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. Points give equal-weight dataset means; horizontal segments give dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in AUC (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

Figure: lgd_sampling_benchmark_credit
LGD. Held-out credit: five-fold benchmark effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. Points give equal-weight dataset means; horizontal segments give dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Fractional RMSE reduction (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Fractional RMSE reduction (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

3. Probability quality, calibration and error metrics
Positive contrasts favor the alternative protocol over one sample. F1 and calibration use validation-selected rules. Brier/log loss, ECE and error metrics retain their distinct scales; absent metrics are not zeros. Reused classical and untuned scores provide context.
Raw predictions are paired by dataset, training partition, outer fold and row. All five folds and exactly matching test rows/targets are required. Mean error is prediction minus observed target: positive means overprediction. Its absolute value can conceal offsetting subgroup errors. Brier/MSE and prediction movement pool rows within each table; tables receive equal weight in summaries. These are observed out-of-fold diagnostics, not squared theoretical bias or context variance.

4. Benchmark quality versus training cost
Quality uses the common dataset cohort; cost matches the same base/protocol and requires all four completed training partitions. Recorded time excludes evaluation and queueing. Equal updates are not equal compute.

Figure: pd_sampling_benchmark_quality_cost
PD. Final benchmark effects versus recorded training time summed over four dataset partitions. Quality gives equally weighted datasets in the common three-protocol cohort; its size is recorded alongside every point. Non-credit effects first average four matched partitions per dataset. Colors identify protocols and marker shapes identify model bases. Evaluation and queueing costs are excluded. This is an observed cost comparison, not a matched-compute experiment or an estimated optimal frontier.

Figure: lgd_sampling_benchmark_quality_cost
LGD. Final benchmark effects versus recorded training time summed over four dataset partitions. Quality gives equally weighted datasets in the common three-protocol cohort; its size is recorded alongside every point. Non-credit effects first average four matched partitions per dataset. Colors identify protocols and marker shapes identify model bases. Evaluation and queueing costs are excluded. This is an observed cost comparison, not a matched-compute experiment or an estimated optimal frontier.

LGD. Ratios to the one-sample trial matched on base, recipe and dataset partition. Only partitions with all three completed protocols enter. Points are partition means and segments are partition interquartile ranges, not uncertainty intervals. Trial time includes recorded monitoring and excludes queueing; it is not billed GPU allocation time. Row exposure counts repeated rows. Absolute costs and peak memory accompany the ratios.

5. Supporting endpoint monitors and interpretation
All three experiment-3 arms share proportional PD sampling. Differences from the balanced-PD main reference cannot be attributed solely to pass mode. Table overlap and overlapping training folds limit independence claims.

Figure: pd_sampling_monitor_credit
PD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. Points give equal-weight dataset means; horizontal segments give dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in AUC (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

LGD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. Points give equal-weight dataset means; horizontal segments give dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in R² (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

Figure: lgd_sampling_monitor_ood
LGD. Non-credit retention: 10000-update monitor effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. Points give equal-weight dataset means; horizontal segments give dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in R² (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.
```

## experiment4/01_context_curves

```
Experiment 4: labeled context and the value of CPT

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Does credit CPT change the value of labeled context on an excluded credit table? Dependence on context size is different from variability across repeated contexts of the same size.

1. Fixed checkpoints and evaluation protocol
The 50,000-row cap bounds computation; it is not TabPFN v3’s native limit. The available-pool endpoint is included when distinct. Validation and test rows never enter context.

Table: Evaluation protocol
CSV (first column: row index)
row,setting,value
0,Models,Explicit TabPFN v3 and TabICLv2 original/CPT pairs
1,CPT source,cpt_main_v5; full updates; LR 3e-07; L2-SP 0.003; seed 42; 10000 updates
2,Dataset exclusion,Each table uses its original experiment-1 held-out partition's checkpoint
3,Outer test folds,5
4,Context rows,"8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096, 6144, 8192, 12288, 16384, 20480, 24576, 32768, 40960, 49152, 50000"
5,Additional endpoint,"Available context pool, capped at 50,000, without duplicate sizes"
6,Validation labels,"Fixed 20% of each outer training fold, separate from context"
7,Test rows,All outer-test rows; unchanged across context budgets and original/CPT
8,Inference views,"{'tabpfn': 32, 'tabicl': 8}"
9,Aggregation,Five paired folds per table; equal-weight table means; fixed cohort within each curve

2. Completed exports and five-fold support
Absent exports are unavailable evidence, not zero performance. DATA plans/receipts and project metric exports are both needed. Coverage counts are not live scheduler status.

3. Original and CPT context curves
Primary scores are PD AUC and LGD R². Scores first average the five paired folds within each table, then weight tables equally. Positive differences favor CPT. No figure is generated for a horizon without a complete common cohort.

Figure: context_pd_through_128
PD. Original and fixed-recipe CPT AUC, with their paired difference below. The same 17 tables contribute at every displayed context size and to both model families. Scores are averaged over five paired outer folds within table, then equally across tables. Validation labels have a fixed additional budget; all outer-test rows are unchanged. The horizon identifies the table cohort, so levels across different horizon panels need not agree.

4. Calibration, errors and inference cost
Brier score, log loss, ECE, RMSE, MAE and elapsed-time gains use original minus CPT; AUC, R² and F1 gains use CPT minus original. Timing includes fitting and validation/test prediction, excludes prior CPT training and queue time, and can be affected by fixed execution order. Fold averages are descriptive, not independent table replications.
```

## experiment5/01_training

```
Experiment 5: DiagScale during continued pretraining

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Can restricting cross-table credit adaptation to query scaling preserve useful in-context behavior? This is fixed-endpoint domain CPT, not target-table validation-selected fine-tuning.

1. Adapter recipe and training coverage
Only optimizer-selected scale deltas are updated. TabICL can retain backbone autograd flags without placing backbone tensors in the optimizer. Completed training does not establish completed evaluation.

Figure: adapter_optimization_pd_v3
PD. Mean diagnostics across all four dataset partitions at each adapter rate. Lines connect recorded summaries, with periodically spaced markers; a missing partition leaves a gap. Data loss is the native query objective; incomplete table-coverage epochs are excluded. Gradient diagnostics concern optimizer-selected query-scale deltas. Movement is RMS delta from the identity scaling, not a relative change from zero-valued adapter parameters.

Movement is RMS delta from the identity scaling, not a relative change from zero-valued adapter parameters.

Figure: adapter_optimization_lgd_v3
LGD. Mean diagnostics across all four dataset partitions at each adapter rate. Lines connect recorded summaries, with periodically spaced markers; a missing partition leaves a gap. Data loss is the native query objective; incomplete table-coverage epochs are excluded. Gradient diagnostics concern optimizer-selected query-scale deltas. Movement is RMS delta from the identity scaling, not a relative change from zero-valued adapter parameters.

3. Credit transfer and non-credit retention
Each table is paired with its own update-zero score. A complete baseline cohort and every planned partition are required. Repeated non-credit observations are averaged within table before equal-table aggregation.

Figure: adapter_monitors_pd
PD. Change in AUC from each table's update-zero score. Repeated non-credit partitions are averaged within table; tables receive equal weight. All planned partitions and the unchanged baseline table cohort are required at every milestone. These fixed-context training monitors are distinct from the final five-fold benchmark.

4. Applied schedule and computational cost
The common schedule is shown once for PD/LGD. Device utilization and memory are sampled observations, not integrated energy. Original-weight preservation is certified by experiment-0 checks, not inferred from low drift. Final predictive comparisons belong in the results notebook.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

Figure: resource_dashboard_pd
Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.

Figure: resource_dashboard_lgd
Device counters during training, summarized first by a within-trial window median, then by the median across observed trials. Recipes and adaptation modes are pooled; trial counts accompany every value. Axes start at zero, and utilization spans 0–100%, so small counter fluctuations are not magnified. Changing support can change these descriptive curves. Device samples are neither process-specific utilization nor integrated energy measurements. Missing counters remain gaps.
```

```
Experiment 5: DiagScale transfer and retention

0. Evidence and scope
DATA: no external source selected.
Project: no external source selected.
Missing project records are unavailable evidence, not zero effects or failed training.
Can restricting cross-table credit adaptation to query scaling preserve useful in-context behavior? This is fixed-endpoint domain CPT, not target-table validation-selected fine-tuning.

Trained and original cells need all five finite outer folds. Non-credit table comparisons additionally require all four training-dataset partitions. Missing cells remain unavailable.

Points are tables, diamonds are equal-table means and vertical bars span the table interquartile range, not confidence intervals. Only tables measured at all three rates enter each model/domain panel; non-credit tables require all four training partitions. Every trained/control pair requires all five finite outer folds. Positive effects favor DiagScale.

3. Probability quality and regression errors
Probabilities are evaluated at test prevalence. F1/calibration rules use inner validation only. RMSE effects are fractional reductions relative to the matched original; other differences retain their metric scale. Unsupported/nonfinite metrics are not filled with zeros.
Raw predictions are paired by dataset, training partition, outer fold and row. All five folds and exactly matching test rows/targets are required. Mean error is prediction minus observed target: positive means overprediction. Its absolute value can conceal offsetting subgroup errors. Brier/MSE and prediction movement pool rows within each table; tables receive equal weight in summaries. These are observed out-of-fold diagnostics, not squared theoretical bias or context variance.

Figure: adapter_benchmark_pd_brier_score
PD. Five-fold paired DiagScale effects relative to the original checkpoint under matched inference precision. Points are tables, diamonds are equal-table means and vertical bars span the table interquartile range, not confidence intervals. Only tables measured at all three rates enter each model/domain panel; non-credit tables require all four training partitions. Every trained/control pair requires all five finite outer folds. Positive effects favor DiagScale.

Figure: lgd_prediction_diagnostics
LGD. Matched five-fold out-of-fold predictions on held-out credit tables. Diamonds are equal-table means; segments are dataset interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals. Each label gives the number of tables. Mean error is predicted minus observed target, pooled over test rows within a table. The left panel measures reduction of its absolute value; the right measures reduction in squared error. These are empirical errors, not a theoretical bias–variance decomposition.

4. Cost and interpretation boundaries
This experiment tests a cross-table DiagScale recipe. It is not a literal reproduction of target-table adapter fine-tuning, nor a pure parameter-count ablation against previous full-update runs. Overlapping training corpora, related data sources and the small retention panel limit independence and generality claims. Report unfavorable outcomes alongside improvements.
```

```
Figure: size_optimization_v3
Native query cross-entropy excludes anchoring. Each line averages the four planned dataset partitions; missing partitions leave gaps. The corpus-policy comparison changes the loss population, so a lower training loss is not by itself evidence of better transfer. Other panels show optimization and movement, not final predictive quality.

Each curve uses fixed table support and matched arms. Non-credit tables require all four training partitions. No final benchmark scores enter these curves.
```
